source.quote: Let δ ∈ (0, 1) and βt = 2 log(|D|t^2 π^2/6δ). Running GP-UCB with βt for a sample f of a GP with mean function zero and covariance function k(x, x'), we obtain a regret bound of O*(sqrt(T γT log |D|)) with high probability. Precisely, Pr{RT ≤ sqrt(C1 T βT γT) ∀T ≥ 1} ≥ 1 − δ. where C1 = 8/log(1 + σ^{-2}).

results.notes: |D| = K. Square root lost in pdftotext; confirmed by proof (R_T^2 <= T sum r_t^2 <= C1 T beta_T gamma_T). gamma_T is maximum information gain (canonical gamma_T). Holds w.p. 1-delta jointly over GP sample and noise, for all T. O*(sqrt(T gamma_T log|D|)) form also stated.

source.quote: Let δ ∈ (0, 1). Assume that the true underlying f lies in the RKHS Hk(D) corresponding to the kernel k(x, x'), and that the noise εt has zero mean conditioned on the history and is bounded by σ almost surely. In particular, assume ||f||_k^2 ≤ B and let βt = 2B + 300γt log^3(t/δ). Running GP-UCB with βt, prior GP(0, k(x, x')) and noise model N(0, σ^2), we obtain a regret bound of O*(sqrt(T)(B sqrt(γT) + γT)) with high probability (over the noise). Precisely, Pr{RT ≤ sqrt(C1 T βT γT) ∀T ≥ 1} ≥ 1 − δ, where C1 = 8/log(1 + σ^{-2}).

results.notes: Paper's B is the squared RKHS norm bound, written as S**2. Square root restored per proof structure. O* form sqrt(T)(B sqrt(gamma_T)+gamma_T) also stated.

source.quote: Together with Theorems 2 and 3, this result guarantees sublinear regret of GP-UCB for any dimension (see Figure 1). For the Squared Exponential kernel, the dimension d appears as exponent of log T only, so that the regret grows at most as O*(sqrt(T)(log T)^{(d+1)/2})

results.notes: Derived in text by combining Theorem 5 (gamma_T = O((log T)^{d+1})) with Theorem 2; O* suppresses log factors (and d, delta dependence).

source.quote: Plugging this in, we have γT = O(T^{1-2η}(log T)), η = ν/(2ν+d(d+1)). Together with Theorem 2 (for ν > 2), we have that RT = O*(T^{1−η}) (suppressing log factors): for any ν > 2 and any dimension d, the GP-UCB algorithm is guaranteed to be no-regret in this case with arbitrarily high probability.

results.notes: Stated in appendix proof of Theorem 5 and in Figure 1; 1-eta = (nu+d(d+1))/(2nu+d(d+1)).
